Nearly half a million Indian schools still have no internet. This is exactly the kind of problem Starlink was built to solve

According to India's Education Ministry’s UDISE+ 2025–26 data:

• 1,466,682 schools nationwide
• 989,191 have internet access
• 477,491 still don't have internet
• Only 67.4% of schools are connected

That means nearly one in three schools across India still lacks internet access

This is where Starlink makes a real difference

For schools in remote villages and regions where laying fiber is difficult or expensive, and so they essentially end up with no internet at all, satellite internet brings teachers and students online without waiting for broadband cables to reach every classroom

And Starlink has already demonstrated what this can achieve

In 2025 alone, Starlink connected more than 6 million students worldwide through education initiatives

India has millions of students living far beyond major cities, and connecting underserved schools would open up access to online learning, educational resources, and opportunities that were previously out of reach

A child's access to knowledge should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom

This is another powerful reason to bring Starlink connectivity to more schools across India

This selloff in memory stocks makes absolutely NO sense to me.

$MU, $SNDK, Samsung and SK Hynix are getting hit after China's CXMT announced progress on its new 4F² DRAM architecture, with plans to introduce DDR5 server memory using the technology by the end of 2026. For those unfamiliar, this technology is designed to pack more memory cells into the same amount of space, potentially improving chip density and manufacturing efficiency.

Now, I want to make something clear. CXMT is absolutely becoming a legitimate competitor because acording to TrendForce, CXMT has already captured roughly 9.5% of global DRAM revenue, up from 7.6% the previous quarter, making it the fourth largest DRAM manufacturer globally. The company is also expanding aggressively, with new manufacturing facilities in Shanghai and Hefei targeting more than 600,000 wafers per month, potentially doubling its manufacturing capacity. On top of that, CXMT has reportedly started mass production of its G5 DRAM platform and LPDDR6 memory, while its new 4F² architecture could make memory production even more efficient.

But here's why I think the market is getting WAY ahead of itself. First, announcing a new memory architecture and successfully manufacturing it at scale are two completely different things. CXMT still needs to prove it can deliver competitive yields, pricing, reliability, and production volumes. Second, we're currently dealing with an enormous memory supply shortage, particularly as hyperscalers continue increasing AI infrastructure spending. Even if CXMT successfully doubles its capacity, that doesn't automatically mean the industry becomes oversupplied. Demand for memory is expected to grow substantially over the next several years, and we're already seeing manufacturers secure longer term supply agreements with customers.

Third, this announcement is primarily focused on conventional DDR5 server memory, NOT HBM. That's an important distinction because HBM is becoming one of the most valuable parts of the memory industry, with Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix benefiting from enormous AI demand. And SanDisk primarily manufactures NAND flash memory, not DRAM. So selling $SNDK specifically because of a DDR5 technology announcement seems even more questionable. Now, that doesn't mean CXMT won't eventually put pressure on conventional DRAM prices. Increased Chinese manufacturing capacity is absolutely something investors should monitor, especially over the longer term but I think investors are confusing a legitimate long term competitive threat with an immediate change in industry fundamentals. Nothing about today's announcement suddenly creates millions of additional memory chips, eliminates existing supply shortages, or changes the amount of memory needed to power AI infrastructure. I've been saying this for months. The amount of memory we're going to need over the next decade is INSANE. A four-hour hit-piece documentary rolling out nationwide. Midterms three weeks away. Every outlet, every NGO, every “expert” panel suddenly singing from the same sheet, on the same day, with the same words.

None of it is spontaneous.

What you are watching is an organism. Call it international socialism, call it the managerial left, the name doesn’t matter. It is a network that spent decades quietly capturing the universities, the newsrooms, the foundations, the administrative state, every institution that was supposed to referee the game instead of playing it.

For years it worked because no one with real power ever looked under the hood.

Then a man who lands rockets, owns the public square and needs nobody’s permission started looking. And started showing everyone else what he found.

So the organism does what every organism does when it senses a threat to its survival. It screams.

Don’t mistake the noise for strength. What you are about to hear is not the roar of a system in control. It is a death cry.

When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example. 

SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does a majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. 

Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast. 

Newer HBM architectures and things like an SRAM layer below logic and 3D stacking RAM on top of logic while finding a way to keep the logic cooled will be harder to solve.

USDD流通量突破18亿美元，年初至今增长262%

再度迎来ATH ，USDD流通量已达到 18.1亿美元，刷新历史最高纪录。USDD年内新增流通量约 13.1亿美元，增幅约 262%，整体规模扩大至年初的3.6倍左右。

今年以来，USDD进一步覆盖TRON、以太坊及BNB Chain等生态，并通过储蓄产品、DeFi协议和零Gas转账等功能，提升了资金使用效率和用户体验。

从7月底约15.8亿美元，到如今突破18亿美元，USDD仍保持较强的增长势头。

一切才刚刚开始。
